predict.prompt: Predict the decisive experimental condition before fully solving: Represent 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O before reaction, as hot vapour and after complete condensation.
predict.defensible_answer: Under the ideal-gas approximation, equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles for comparable gas mixtures. This underlies the use of gaseous volume ratios from balanced reaction coefficients when all reacting and measured species remain gases at the same reference T/P. For example, 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g) gives two gas-volume units H₂ and one O₂ forming two units of water vapour at comparable conditions. If water condenses, the measured gas volume is no longer two units.

asks.ask: Which gases are present and which quantities were measured?
asks.model_response: An unknown gas mixture burns, cools, then passes through a selective absorber. A single number called 'contraction' appears on the instrument. Can it reveal a complete molecular formula by itself?

asks.ask: Which conditions and chemical equation or apparatus model hold?
asks.why_this_ask: Build a warranted model instead of a contraction trick.
asks.model_response: To analyse a hydrocarbon CₓHᵧ, use the complete-combustion equation and amount ledger. At consistent T/P, CO₂ produced is proportional to x times hydrocarbon amount, while O₂ consumed is proportional to (x + y/4). A single contraction value may not determine both x and y; an independent measurement of CO₂, O₂ consumption or initial hydrocarbon volume can provide further constraints. When an absorber's chemistry is not selective, the problem may remain underdetermined.

boundary_test.answer: Yes, and it must appear in the species ledger.
